bias.headline: Conditions are clearly bullish (led by Risk Appetite) — on thin evidence, so treat the description itself as tentative. This describes the current state, not a prediction.

topBullish.label: Risk Appetite
topBullish.confidenceBasis: 500 prior sessions of the same credit-minus-duration spread; the current reading is at its 85th percentile.
topBullish.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are beating safe government bonds by 3.1% — money is willing to take risk to earn more, which usually accompanies a rising stock market.
topBullish.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.
topBullish.nextTrigger: stops being bullish if it falls out of the top third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 85% of them

topBullish.label: Market Breadth
topBullish.confidenceBasis: 95 individual companies, each counted once, against 500 sessions of this panel's own breadth history. A participation count rather than an index proxy — but still a large-cap panel, not a full advance/decline line, so confidence is capped at 75.
topBullish.explanation: 71% of 95 companies are trading above their own 50-session average. That is unusually broad — higher than 73% of its own past readings for this group, whose typical session reads 62%.
topBullish.whyItMatters: A rally carried by one or two names is fragile in a way the index level does not show. Broad participation is what separates a durable advance from a narrow one.
topBullish.nextTrigger: stops being bullish if it falls out of the top third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 73% of them

topBullish.label: Volatility
topBullish.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
topBullish.explanation: SPY typically moves 0.98% in a day right now — more volatile than 27% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.
topBullish.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
topBullish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 27% of them

watchNext.label: Trend Strength

watchNext.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.15 now

metrics.explanation: Over 60 sessions IWM moved +12.0%, and only 21% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a real direction, but a choppy one.
metrics.whyItMatters: Direction alone does not say whether a move is worth following. The same net return produced by a straight line and by a round trip demand different trades; efficiency is what separates them.
metrics.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.21 now

metrics.label: Market Structure
metrics.confidenceBasis: 10 swing highs and 8 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 28% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
metrics.explanation: IWM is printing higher highs but lower lows — a broadening range, not a trend. Last swing high 301.71 vs prior 293.37; last swing low 288.57 vs prior 289.88.
metrics.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
conflicts: Highs are rising while lows are falling: volatility is expanding without direction.
metrics.nextTrigger: resolves on a close outside 288.57–301.71

metrics.label: Risk Appetite
metrics.confidenceBasis: 500 prior sessions of the same credit-minus-duration spread; the current reading is at its 85th percentile.
metrics.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are beating safe government bonds by 3.1% — money is willing to take risk to earn more, which usually accompanies a rising stock market.
metrics.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bullish if it falls out of the top third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 85% of them

metrics.label: Volatility
metrics.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
metrics.explanation: IWM typically moves 1.24% in a day right now — more volatile than 0% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.
metrics.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 0% of them
